critical_evidence.evidence: No borescope or engine rebuild record is provided. A commenter asked for borescope or oil-analysis history and no answer is shown. Seller statements would not count anyway.
No DME over-rev report is provided or mentioned.

The Carfax shows only 1 service record over ~19 years. No invoices exist for coolant, water pump, AOS, clutch or fluids. No reported entry does not mean the work was not done, but nothing documents it.

documentation.rationale: The identity half is present: VIN with a clean decode, Carfax snapshot, clean MA title claim, and a full option list. The maintenance half is absent: one Carfax service record, no invoices, no borescope, no DME report.

condition.rationale: Photos show tidy paint, a lightly worn interior and a clean rear subframe area. The disclosed headliner sag is cosmetic. The ~500 miles in 10 years implies long storage with unknown fluid, tire and seal ages. Nothing proves engine condition either way.

price_value.rationale: The $10k current bid is meaningless with a reserve. Low-mileage S comps cluster around $27.5k–$42k against a fair value of $30.1k–$37.0k, so it will likely close near fair value. That price buys an S with zero engine due diligence plus storage catch-up.

mission_fit.rationale: It is a manual Cayman, which fits the keeper category. However, the profile requires unusually strong engine due diligence for a 3.4 S, and none exists. The likely hammer also sits high in the budget band against cash preservation.

logistics.rationale: Raynham, MA is far from Carmel, and under 22 hours remain. The seller is open to viewings, but a specialist PPI and borescope before money moves is unlikely in that window. BaT shipping is available.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Manual S with Sport Chrono, PASM, bi-xenons and 19-inch Carrera S wheels at low miles is desirable. Black over black standard leather is common rather than rare.

ppi_focus: Specialist borescope of all cylinders, with emphasis on 4–6, retaining photos
PIWIS DME over-rev report and fault-code scan
Compression/leakdown read alongside the borescope, not instead of it
Oil filter cut and oil analysis for metal or plastic debris
Cold-start smoke and AOS function (smoke on start-up, idle quality, oil-cap vacuum)
Coolant pipes, water pump weep and radiator condition after long storage
Clutch engagement point and dual-mass flywheel noise
Tire date codes and age-hardening; brake fluid moisture
Underside corrosion check for a New England car: subframes, brake lines, suspension hardware
Headliner and any water ingress around the rear hatch seals
what_would_change_verdict: A clean specialist borescope of cylinders 4–6 plus a clean DME over-rev report would materially strengthen documentation and the keeper case.
Invoices showing recent water pump, AOS, coolant and fluids would raise documentation and condition.
Scoring evidence, over-rev range 1+ counts, or leaks found at inspection would move it sharply down.
A hammer well below the $30k–$37k fair value band would improve value, though it would not offset missing engine evidence.
Tires with old date codes would add a known replacement cost.
evidence.mission_note: A manual Cayman S fits the future-keeper category, but the profile buys a 3.4 S only with unusually strong engine due diligence, and this listing offers none. A likely hammer near fair value also sits high in the budget band against current cash preservation, so it is attractive only as a keeper.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: a VIN that decodes to a 2007 Cayman S coupe, a well-optioned manual car with Sport Chrono and PASM, a Carfax with no reported accidents, and a mileage reading of 26,370 consistent with the 27k claim. It establishes almost no maintenance history: one Carfax service record across six owners and ~19 years, no invoices, no borescope, and no DME over-rev report. The only observed fault is the disclosed sagging headliner. About 500 miles in the last ~10 years signals long storage, so age-related items are open questions despite the low mileage. A bidder has already asked for borescope and service history without a shown reply. Photos show a well-kept exterior and interior and a clean rear subframe area, with only surface rust on the muffler. Comparable low-mileage S cars put the likely close around fair value of roughly $30k–$37k. With under 22 hours left and the car in Massachusetts, inspection before close is the binding constraint.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller now asking whether a specialist borescope and PIWIS over-rev report can be done in Raynham before the close, and line up a New England Porsche specialist to do them.
